items.key: ai:no one expected an american pope. here's the inside story of how 'bob' became pope leo
items.text: No one expected an American pope. Here's the inside story of how 'Bob' became Pope Leo
items.article: When the 2025 conclave began, no one expected an American pope. But by its end, Cardinal Robert Prevost had become Pope Leo. Here's a look behind the scenes. Robert Prevost is seen in the Vatican's St. Peter's Square as he attends the funeral of Pope Francis on April 26, 2025. The next month, Prevost would be elected the first American pope, becoming Pope Leo. Franco Origlia/Getty Images hide caption NPR's Daniel Burke and Scott Detrow covered the 2025 conclave that elected Pope Leo XIV. The following excerpt is adapted from their new biography of Pope Leo, American Pope , out Tuesday . In the days immediately following Pope Francis' death, messages from friends poured into Cardinal Robert Prevost's phone. Father Ramiro Castillo Castro, who had studied under Prevost in the 1990s, was among those who sent condolences. "Thank you, Ramiro," Prevost responded. "We have to pray a lot. Big hug." "Polly and I send our love and prayers for you in these momentous days," wrote John Snider, a Lutheran pastor with whom Prevost had spent a summer in Minneapolis debating theology and learning how to minister to the sick and dying before they were both ordained. Now, decades later, Snider was winding down his career, and Prevost was about to participate in a conclave to elect the next pope. "As I near retirement, 3 weeks, you are taking on such intense responsibility," he wrote. "God is with you!"

items.text: SF's favorite ice cream sandwich just made a big change
items.article: The mint flavor of San Francisco's favorite It's-It ice cream cookie sandwiches has changed color. A major change has come for San Francisco’s beloved It’s-It ice cream sandwiches. The mint flavor of the ice cream cookie sandwich , once an ostentatiously loud shade of green, has changed color, as first spotted by the San Francisco Chronicle. (The Chronicle and SFGATE are both owned by Hearst but have separate newsrooms.) An SFGATE editor bought a box at Andronico’s and confirmed the breaking news — the bright, toothpaste-green ice cream had been drained of color, with a far more muted, pale pastel green in its place. Where the shade once screamed “GREEN!” at the top of its lungs, now, it only whispered. Curiously, though, It’s-It has mostly kept the change quiet. Despite SFGATE’s repeated attempts this week to reach the Burlingame-based company for comment, It’s-It never got back to us. The company has not released any statement announcing the change to its customers, and photos of the mint ice cream sandwich on its website remain the same , advertising the old seafoam green color instead of the new, lighter shade. It’s-It President Charles Shamieh did speak with the Chronicle, telling the outlet that It’s-It made the change due to U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. items.article: Smit Machchhar says in video call with Indian PM that he realised if he did not get up ‘passengers would lose their lives’ The Indian pilot who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv said his faith and his desire to save his passengers allowed him to make a “last push” to open the cockpit door as he fought for his life. Capt Smit Machchhar, who was recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, described to India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, how he helped save the plane and its more than 170 passengers. “I had suffered so many injuries that I had collapsed. At that time, I could feel that the aircraft was going down. I knew this was the last push,” Machchhar told Modi in a video call on Friday. “I was fighting for my life. At one point, I realised that if I didn’t get up … then passengers would lose their lives.” His Omani co-pilot apparently stabbed him and set the plane on a steep descent, with the aircraft plummeting about 17,000 feet in the span of a minute. While still being attacked, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter, subdue the attacker and ultimately stabilise the plane. The full circumstances of the attack are still under investigation, but a relief crew on the flight helped land the plane safely in Tabouk, north-west Saudi Arabia .
